name: blastem
why: A fast, accurate Genesis emulator whose cycle-accurate internals reward watching old 68000 code run.

brief.what_it_is: BlastEm is a free and open source emulator for Sega's 16-bit and 8-bit consoles. Per its homepage, its primary focus is the Genesis (Mega Drive outside North America), and it also lists support for the Sega CD, 32X, Master System, Game Gear, SG-1000, SC-3000, Sega Pico and Yamaha Copera. The homepage does not describe its inputs or outputs in detail beyond running these systems' software.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage pitches it as an emulator that is both fast and accurate: fast enough for modest old PCs, and accurate enough for demanding demos and synthetic accuracy tests. It says the first emulator to properly run Titan's Overdrive 2 demo was BlastEm.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no installation steps, requirements, or first-run configuration. The brew formula's executable is 'blastem'. The README/docs that would cover this were not reachable (see fetch_log).
brief.standout: The homepage claims top-tier accuracy without needing a high-end machine: it says BlastEm was developed on a 2011 netbook-class laptop and still runs Genesis emulation at full speed there. It also says it was the first emulator to run Overdrive 2 properly.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage has no release dates, changelog, or last-updated note, and I could not reach a source repository to check commits or releases.
brief.caveats: I could not read a README or documentation, so platform support, build requirements, licensing details beyond 'free and Open Source', and missing features are not confirmed. The homepage's accuracy claims are the project's own framing, not independently verified here. The homepage also lists systems beyond the Genesis, but the text says the Genesis is the primary focus.
quotes: an emulator for Sega's 16-bit and 8-bit consoles
fast enough for your old PC
accurate enough for the most demanding demos
